judgments.reasoning_cat1: A benefit-of, no-marshalling and reinstatement clause; long but each element is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 16.7's revival provision and Section 14.1's assignment mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard subrogation/contribution deferral; the drafting is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.13(b), (k) and 2.3(b)'s waterfall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two parallel undertakings plus a trustee mechanism; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs collected amounts to be applied under Section 2.3(b), which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The chapeau's deeming rule (making the initial extension of credit "conclusively deemed" to be satisfaction or waiver of everything) is a powerful provision, but it is expressed unambiguously.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Section 3.3's ongoing conditions and Section 3.2's conditions subsequent without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of six documents subject to Lender's satisfaction; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits the Filing Authorization Letter (covered in (a)) and does not require a Subordination Agreement or Guaranty though both are defined; a gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It speaks of each Borrower's "Board of Directors" and "officers" although both Borrowers are limited liability companies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Board of Directors definition expressly extends to comparable LLC managers, which cures the mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short delivery condition; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Governing Documents definition and Section 7.3(a)'s bar on amending them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The certificate must be "dated within 36 days of the Closing Date", a figure that appears nowhere else and looks like a slip for 30 days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The immediately following clause (f) requires the parallel foreign certificates to be dated within 30 days, so the two adjacent conditions use different periods for the same purpose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The universe of jurisdictions is defined by whether non-qualification "would constitute a Material Adverse Change", importing that vague standard into a mechanical delivery condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 30 days where clause (e) uses 36; otherwise consistent with Section 5.8(a)'s qualification representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A delivery condition tied to Section 6.8's requirements; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(a) sets out the insurance and endorsement requirements referenced; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]n opinion of Borrowers' and Servicer's counsel in form and substance satisfactory to Lender" leaves the content entirely open, but that is the ordinary form of such a condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision specifies the opinion's contents; a gap without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]atisfactory evidence" of tax filings and payment, with a Permitted Protest carve-out; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.7's tax covenant and the Permitted Protest definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "the Loewe-Adler collateral review", an extrinsic document not defined or attached, and every element ends in "satisfactory to Lender".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The condition overlaps with Section 3.1(m) (Required Procedures) and 3.1(p) (loan documentation forms) without delimiting the boundary between them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Results must be "satisfactory to Lender in its sole discretion" — an unqualified subjective standard, unlike "Permitted Discretion" used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four named individuals match the Permitted Holders definition but omit Stephanie Ng Kelly, who is an Executive Officer and Validity Agreement Party; a small inconsistency in the cast of key people.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall have paid or shall pay with the initial Advance" makes a condition precedent capable of satisfaction simultaneously with, or after, the event it conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.5(c)'s authority to charge Lender Expenses to the Loan Account as Advances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short approval condition; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower's Required Procedures definition presupposes exactly this pre-closing approval; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dollar test on a named date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 7.16(a)'s $600,000,000 ongoing floor exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires a "Landlord's Waiver and Consent", a capitalised phrase that is not a defined term anywhere in the agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term for this instrument is "Collateral Access Agreement" (used in Section 6.9), so the condition uses a label the rest of the instrument does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Satisfaction is measured by whether counsel is "satisfied that such documentation provides Fund and Lender with appropriate rights and remedies" — "appropriate" is soft but the condition is Lender-facing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 3.1(m)'s approval of the same form documents; duplicative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso allows the entire regulatory-compliance condition to be satisfied by "such reasonable assurances as Lender may require", which largely dissolves the condition it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 makes the same compliance a flat representation with no assurance substitute, so the condition and the representation are calibrated differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A due-diligence review condition entirely in Lender's satisfaction; conventional for a closing condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses these reviews; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies specific financial statements by period; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.11's financial-statement representation and Section 6.3's ongoing reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It conditions the *initial* extension of credit on delivery "no less than two (2) Business Days preceding the date of such Advance", although "such Advance" has no antecedent in Section 3.1, and item (iii) requires a title policy that clause (r)(v) of Eligible Notes Receivable allows to be a pro forma or marked commitment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The eight-item list here differs materially from the nine-item list in the Eligible Notes Receivable definition clause (r) (which adds recorded collateral assignments and hazard insurance evidence), yet Sections 3.3(e), 4.2 and 8.17 all measure compliance by reference to this list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ll other documents and legal matters ... in form and substance satisfactory to Lender" is an unlimited residual condition sitting after twenty specific ones — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the chapeau's deemed-waiver rule the risk is contained, but the catch-all would otherwise swallow the enumerated conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is mis-numbered "4.2" in the text and reads "Manager shall have a hired a full time Controller"; the single condition is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(c) makes failure to satisfy "a condition subsequent set forth in Section 3.2" a default after 20 Business Days, while this chapeau says such failure itself constitutes an Event of Default — the cure periods do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bring-down condition with a materiality qualifier and an earlier-date carve-out; standard and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5's chapeau states the same bring-down, and the Compliance Certificate paragraphs 2 and 5 restate it twice with slightly different carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line no-default condition; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Default and Event of Default definitions and Section 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]o injunction, writ, restraining order, or other order of any nature" — a catch-all after specifics, but the operative limit (restricting the extension of credit) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.6's analogous default; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]o Material Adverse Change shall have occurred" states no baseline date, so it is unclear whether the comparison is to the Closing Date, the last financial statements, or the immediately preceding Advance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.11 measures material adverse change "since the date of the latest financial statements submitted to Lender on or before the Closing Date", which supplies a baseline this condition omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quantified possession requirement plus "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender", which qualifies an otherwise hard number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same $250,000,000 test appears in Sections 3.1(t), 4.2 and 8.17 with slightly different formulations of who must hold the documents and when.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] current Borrowing Base Certificate" — "current" is undefined, though Section 6.2 sets the delivery cadence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The certificate's form is "to be provided by Lender" per Exhibit B-2 and does not exist in the executed document, which weakens this condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed three-year term with an immediate-termination right on an Event of Default, qualified by "subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided"; the qualifier is slightly at odds with "immediately and without notice".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1(b)-(c) also give termination rights on default and Section 3.7(b) prices a Lender-elected termination, so the termination scheme is spread over three provisions but is reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is numbered "3.4" although Section 3.4 (Term) already exists; it is an intentionally blank section with a duplicated number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Maturity Date definition and Section 3.7(b) cross-refer to Section 3.4, which now points at two different provisions — a real, if easily resolved, cross-reference problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceleration on termination plus survival of Liens and duties; the release obligation is conditioned in detail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires cash collateral for Bank Product Obligations consistently with Sections 3.7(a) and 2.3(b), and with Section 1.4's gloss on repayment in full.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 30-day notice option with a fully specified payoff; the cash collateral amount is set by Lender's determination of "reasonably estimated credit exposure".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6 and 3.7(b) and the Applicable Prepayment Premium definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference is garbled ("Section 3.'M(a)"), and the liquidated-damages recital is coupled with "if applicable", leaving unclear whether the premium is owed at all where the Applicable Prepayment Premium has fallen to zero.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes the premium on terminations arising from foreclosure or plan confirmation in an Insolvency Proceeding, which must be squared with Section 3.6's automatic acceleration and the zero-percent second-year premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is over "Borrower Collateral" but the final sentence bars disposition of "the Collateral", a wider defined term; the switch mid-provision is noticeable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Collateral" is defined to include assets of Subsidiaries subject to Liens under other Loan Documents, yet only Borrowers grant here; Sections 7.4 and the Permitted Dispositions definition supply the exceptions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery trigger is conditioned on Lender's determination that possession is needed, then a flat $250,000,000 holding requirement is imposed; the sentence "If Event of Default has occurred" is missing an article.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e), 6.16 and 8.17 all address the same $250,000,000 delivery requirement in overlapping but non-identical terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated post-default powers plus a trust obligation for Collections; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The trust obligation duplicates Section 2.6(a)(ii)'s deposit requirement and Section 9.1(e)'s collection rights, but does not conflict with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard UCC filing authorisation and ratification; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Filing Authorization Letter definition and Section 3.1(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise three-Business-Day obligation with a defined output document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.7(d)'s representation and Borrower Collateral clause (c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]nd all other documents ... that Lender may request in its Permitted Discretion" is an open-ended catch-all after a list of specific instruments, and the copyright registration proviso is dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates perfecting Liens on "any owned Real Property acquired after the Closing Date" although Real Property is not an enumerated item of Borrower Collateral; the two provisions have to be read together to work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An assignment of access rights with a post-default entry right; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.5's and Section 7.15's public-warehouse provisos, which contemplate assigned access.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Powers (b), (e) and (f) are limited to periods when an Event of Default is continuing while (a), (c) and (d) are not, an asymmetry easy to dispute; "irrevocable" appointment is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (a) permits signature of Section 4.4 documents at any time, which is broader than Section 4.4(c)'s own authorisation to execute Additional Documents; substantially consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Inspection rights bounded by "normal business hours" and "reasonable notice"; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.10(d) prices these audits and appraisals and Section 6.5(c) adds appraiser access; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny or all reasonable steps" is a slightly odd formulation, but the Code sections identified make the obligation concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The liquidation right is triggered by a mere Default here, whereas most other remedies require an Event of Default; a notable but express difference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening clause ("Until such time as the Lender shall notify ... of the revocation of such right after the occurrence and during the continuation of an Event of Default") is tangled, and servicing may include "such action ... as the Borrowers may deem advisable".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Revocation must be given "in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement", an instrument not in the record, while Section 9.1(e)(ii) lets Lender terminate that agreement outright — two different routes to the same result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires return of a note that has been "repaid in its entirety" so as "to facilitate its payment", which is internally inconsistent about sequence, and then releases Liens only on receipt of final payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 requires Lender to hold at least $250,000,000 of Eligible Notes Receivable at all times, so returning repaid notes must be reconciled with that floor and with Section 8.17's cure mechanism.
